title: National Plumbing Code Fixture Units and Venting
subject: Building Utilities

questions.stem: In the Revised National Plumbing Code definition, one fixture unit is equivalent to what flow rate?

rationale.correct: The definition states that one fixture unit is equivalent to a rate of flow at 28.3 liters per minute (1 cu. ft./minute).

distractors.A: 10.7 is not the cited plumbing fixture-unit equivalent; the local fixture-unit definition points to 28.3 L/min.

rationale.takeaway: Fixture unit is a load/flow scale, and the cited equivalent is 28.3 L/min.

questions.source_locator: Revised National Plumbing Code, Section 207.8, Fixture Unit, PDF p.24.

questions.stem: Which statement follows Section 311.4 of the Revised National Plumbing Code?

options.A: A vent pipe may be used as a soil pipe if it is oversized.
options.B: A soil or waste pipe may be used as a vent if the branch is short.
options.C: No vent pipe shall be used as a soil or waste pipe, nor shall any soil or waste pipe be used as a vent, except as provided in the cited Code sections.
options.D: Single drainage and venting systems with unvented branch lines are allowed for small buildings.

rationale.correct: Section 311.4 states the prohibition and points to exceptions in Sections 812, 813, and 814.

distractors.A: Oversizing is not the stated permission.
distractors.B: Branch length is not the stated permission.
distractors.D: The same section says single drainage and venting systems with unvented branch lines are prohibited.

rationale.takeaway: Do not turn a vent into drainage or drainage into venting unless the Code exception is actually cited.

questions.source_locator: Revised National Plumbing Code, Section 311.4, PDF p.44.

questions.stem: A loop or circuit vent connects on a horizontal soil or waste branch at what location?

options.A: Upstream of the first fixture only
options.B: At a point downstream of the last fixture connection
options.D: At the fixture trap seal only

rationale.correct: The Code definition places the vertical vent connection downstream of the last fixture connection.

distractors.A: The definition says downstream of the last fixture, not upstream of the first.
distractors.D: The definition is not limited to the trap seal.

rationale.takeaway: For loop or circuit vent questions, locate the last fixture connection first.

questions.source_locator: Revised National Plumbing Code, Definitions, Loop or Circuit Vent, PDF p.29.
